A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sine-activated low-rank research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, allowing reliable matching despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original ViT training, GLUE fine-tuning, LLFF reconstruction and Thai Statue occupancy results, together with frequency ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds LLaMA 3-8B, sine-DoRA, ConvNeXt, additional shape-reconstruction and resource-cost results. Some DoRA baseline scores are explicitly attributed to prior work.

M1.justification: The core sine transformation in Equation 3 is unchanged. Appendix A.2.1 adds a sine-DoRA variant that applies this transformation to the direction update within DoRA's magnitude/direction parameterization. Newly specified gain and frequency choices are implementation disclosures rather than evidence of a redesigned core method.

E1.justification: v2 adds commonsense evaluation on BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c and OBQA. Occupancy evaluations expand from Thai Statue to include Lucy and Dragon. The original GLUE, image-classification and LLFF coverage remains; ConvNeXt uses the already evaluated CIFAR100 dataset.

E2.justification: v2 adds DoRA comparisons in Table 7, implementing the rank-8 baseline and using cited results at ranks 16 and 32. It also removes the unactivated low-rank reference from the ViT frequency comparison, formerly v1 Table 5 and now v2 Table 10. Existing principal LoRA, low-rank and full-rank comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include LLaMA 3-8B adaptation of five attention/MLP modules at ranks 4–32 and ConvNeXt-Tiny experiments decomposing the final stage's linear layers with a 150-epoch training budget. DoRA introduces additional rank/configuration comparisons. These extend evaluation substantially; newly disclosed settings for retained experiments do not establish that those experiments changed or were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices A.2.1 and A.2.4 add training-memory measurements for LLaMA and NeRF, plus LLaMA training-time comparisons, testing practical overhead beyond parameter counts. The existing activation comparisons and ViT, NeRF and occupancy frequency sweeps are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 Section 4.2 explicitly states that GLUE results average five random seeds. v2 retains those scores but removes this statement without supplying replacement run-count or uncertainty information. This is reduced statistical reporting, not evidence that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: v2 adds LLaMA/DoRA, ConvNeXt, Lucy/Dragon and resource-cost results. Retained GLUE scores are unchanged. NeRF improvement entries are corrected from 3.12 to 3.10 at rank 5 and 0.74 to 0.77 at rank 60. ViT training-loss entries disappear when the tables become plots. New Table 2 contains a rank-16 delta inconsistency: 84.35 minus 82.90 equals 1.45, although 2.45 is reported.

T1.justification: Proposition 1, Theorem 1, both supporting lemmas and their proof arguments are substantively unchanged. Appendix A.1 adds an explicit reminder of the operator norm already used in the proofs and explanatory remarks, without a new theorem, revised assumption or corrected derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that sinusoidal activation increases low-rank matrices' rank without additional trainable parameters and improves performance across language, vision and 3D applications. Rewritten contributions emphasize its drop-in character, while the expanded experiments support the existing broad applicability claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds discussion of small or zero frequencies, explains frequency-induced gradient amplification and the gain factor's stabilizing role, and explicitly acknowledges that frequency selection lacks a principled rule and requires tuning. The principal limitation concerning the remaining accuracy gap to full-rank models is retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 supplies previously unspecified gain scaling, experiment-specific frequencies, learning rates, epochs and batch sizes, alongside codebase, hardware and timing information. This substantially expands reproducibility documentation. One disclosure remains unclear: Table 13 associates Thai Statue rank-1 IoU 90.8 with frequency 200, whereas retained Figure 9 places that value near frequency 700.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning and citations involving DoRA and circular-convolution parameter-efficient fine-tuning, plus references supporting ConvNeXt, commonsense datasets and implementation choices. The existing low-rank decomposition and parameter-efficient learning discussion is largely retained; bibliography-format and publication-metadata changes do not constitute new positioning.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, revises introduction/contribution and conclusion passages, places language-model experiments before ViT, and reorganizes appendices around application-specific experiments. These are localized narrative and structural revisions; much of the existing methodological and interpretive prose remains close to v1.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a four-application overview, ViT tables become performance-versus-parameter plots, and the full NeRF image grid moves to the appendix while selected examples join a redrawn rate-distortion plot. Numerous new tables, an expanded occupancy table, revised plot styling and the conference-template layout substantially alter presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's sparse implementation documentation by specifying gain, frequencies and training settings, while resource measurements make practical efficiency assessable. LLaMA/DoRA and ConvNeXt experiments strengthen support beyond the earlier model and comparator coverage. These gains outweigh the loss of five-seed disclosure and ViT training-loss values, although the new numerical and frequency inconsistencies limit confidence in some details.
